With school picking back up for Fall, What's some of Voat's favorite recipes for a college student living on the cheap (+-$20) home cooking meal ideas?

One thing I've started cooking a lot is chicken thighs. Brown them in the pan, throw in some teriyaki sauce or balsamic vinager when they're almost done, serve with brown rice. Cheap, get your protein, and taste pretty awesome.

Shove 2 cups of rice, a tin of tomatoes, a tin of lentils / beans, frozen or fresh spinach, peas and cauliflower (or whatever you have in the freezer), water and a stock cube into a rice cooker. Stir it all a bit and turn it on. Add cheese to serve. It's cheap, nutritious and dead easy.

The ApocaSkillet

1 tin of Spam, cubed, and browned in a skillet with veg oil. Add one can of corn (drained) and brown over high heat with the Spam. Add one can of chili beans. Add salt, pepper, cayenne pepper powder, tabasco to taste. Simmer for 10 - 20 minutes. Serve over steamed white long grain rice Light emergency candles.

Here's a couple:

chicken fried rice: cook your rice the night before, refrigerate The next day, throw some oil and garlic in a pan. Add rice, chicken and a bag of frozen assorted veggies (peas, carrots, green beans). crack a couple eggs towards the end, too. Delicious, pretty cheap and fairly easy.

ghetto chicken cordon bleu: take chicken breasts, slice in half, but not all the way - just so you can open them, fill them and close them up again. buy some ham at the store and some string cheese. slice up and stuff in the chicken. sprinkle some bread crumbs on it and bake it up. goes pretty good with rice and broccoli.

If you let even cheap marinara sauce simmer for an hour or so it becomes very tasty. You can add meat (chicken, sausage, ground beef, etc) and put it over noodles or on bread or over many veggies for an easy meal.

Potatoes with skin and chicken.

You can pull a lot of variety from those, some of my favorites are potatoes baked with some thyme shoved inside them then served with light peppering alongside chicken pan-fried in vegetable oil with pepper/salt and a sprig or two of rosemary for flava

Super cheap to buy, filling, relatively nutritionally sound I think (fuck if I know for sure I never studied the stuff just listened to people in the interwebs) and if you start a simple windowsill herb garden (variety pack of seeds is about four bucks I think) you can keep your palate from getting bored by swapping out what you put in from week to week. Also candles are relatively inexpensive so light-em up and prepare for snuggles.

Also: Google sexy pancakes.
Well, I make breakfast burritos in quantity (20+) and freeze them. You can make em for a couple bucks a peice if your careful.
Check out BudgetBytes for cheap and awesome recipes with everything priced out. The Pad Thai is my favorite.

Pasta based dishes are incredibly easy and cheap to make. Switch it up between tomato sauce and pesto. Meatballs or Tilapia can be a decent source of protein.

For your fancy candle lit meal: If you're going for fancy,

  1. Cheap aparativ with a 5 buck preseco

  2. Antipasto is quite cheap to make if you're willing to sacrifice meat quality, salad material is cheap if you are buying bulk (you can use it in other salads)

  3. Pasta main dish (Primo)

  4. Tilapia as a Cod subsitute (secondo)

  5. Salte Veggies as a side dish

  6. two scoop of ice cream/sorbe (dolce)

all of this can be done for under 20 bucks if the ingredients are used for other meals during the week.

If you have time on the weekends, but no time during the week: giant pot of chicken Chile Verde. Make them on the weekend and it'll last the whole week.

Remember, eggs are your friend. (Nutritious and cheap, probably one of the MOST versatile culinary item) Learn to poach them, make proper omlets, or stirfry them with other things, it goes long ways.

Another easy go to is Indian Curry. Make a giant portion of it on the weekend, freeze the rest. Take out what you need during the week and you can make chicken or vegetable curries with them. Just a heads up, your house will smell like curry for DAYS.

Make pancakes from scratch. Super simple. 2 cup self raising flour, 1 cup milk, 1/2 cup of sugar, 1 egg. Whisk and cook in a pan with a little butter. This will make enough to serve two. You can also add some cinnamon or vanilla to mix it up a bit. BAM! Super cheap breakfast.
Also, get a crock pot if you don't already have one. When I was a student that was a huge help. Throw stuff in the morning, go to class, come home to a nice cooked meal.
Spam-fried rice with finely diced Spam, browned, and white rice cooked in broth or boullion and then cooled. Stir fry chopped veggies with a scrambled egg and a lot of soy sauce.

I've found that the Bacon, Lettuce and Tomato sandwich is the Nectar of the Gods, and not too expensive if you buy the right bacon.

Mac N Cheese isn't actually far from greatness. Take your cooked noodles and sprinkle lemon pepper, bacon bits, chives, garlic, and red pepper. It's actually delicious!

If you want to know how to make a more wholesome meals, put a lot of salt on a chicken breast and sweat it in a pan. When all those juices come out, dice the chicken and add fat, pepper, and a buttload of garlic to the juices, and then serve the chicken on some noodles with the sauce ladled over. Really good shit man.

Finally, pancakes are fucking awesome and you should eat more of them.
